requirements.quote:
A UDP datagram can include one or more QUIC packets.  The datagram
   size refers to the total UDP payload size of a single UDP datagram
   carrying QUIC packets.  The datagram size includes one or more QUIC
   packet headers and protected payloads, but not the UDP or IP headers.
requirements.condition: When calculating the datagram size of a UDP datagram carrying QUIC packets.
requirements.required_behavior: Calculate the datagram size as the total UDP payload size, including all QUIC packet headers and protected payloads in that single UDP datagram.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not include UDP or IP headers in the datagram size.
requirements.why_checkable: An implementation's size calculation can be checked against the encoded UDP payload and its protocol headers.

requirements.quote:
The maximum datagram size is defined as the largest size of UDP
   payload that can be sent across a network path using a single UDP
   datagram.  QUIC MUST NOT be used if the network path cannot support a
   maximum datagram size of at least 1200 bytes.
requirements.condition: The network path cannot support a maximum UDP payload size of at least 1200 bytes in one UDP datagram.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: QUIC must not be used on that network path.
requirements.why_checkable: Path capability can be established and the implementation can be observed to reject or avoid QUIC when the maximum supported datagram size is below 1200 bytes.

requirements.quote:
UDP datagrams MUST NOT be fragmented at the IP layer.  In IPv4
   [IPv4], the Don't Fragment (DF) bit MUST be set if possible, to
   prevent fragmentation on the path.
requirements.condition: When sending UDP datagrams carrying QUIC packets.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The UDP datagrams must not be fragmented at the IP layer.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet capture or sender instrumentation can determine whether emitted UDP datagrams are IP-fragmented.

requirements.quote:
UDP datagrams MUST NOT be fragmented at the IP layer.  In IPv4
   [IPv4], the Don't Fragment (DF) bit MUST be set if possible, to
   prevent fragmentation on the path.
requirements.condition: When sending a QUIC UDP datagram over IPv4 and setting the Don't Fragment bit is possible.
requirements.required_behavior: Set the IPv4 Don't Fragment (DF) bit.
requirements.why_checkable: The DF flag on emitted IPv4 packets can be inspected when the platform provides the ability to set it.

requirements.quote:
QUIC sometimes requires datagrams to be no smaller than a certain
   size; see Section 8.1 as an example.  However, the size of a datagram
   is not authenticated.  That is, if an endpoint receives a datagram of
   a certain size, it cannot know that the sender sent the datagram at
   the same size.  Therefore, an endpoint MUST NOT close a connection
   when it receives a datagram that does not meet size constraints; the
   endpoint MAY discard such datagrams.
requirements.condition: An endpoint receives a datagram that does not meet an applicable size constraint.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The endpoint must not close the connection because of the datagram's size-constraint violation.
requirements.error_behavior: Connection closure must not be used to handle the size-constraint violation.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can deliver an undersized or otherwise size-nonconforming datagram and verify that the connection remains open.

requirements.quote:
QUIC sometimes requires datagrams to be no smaller than a certain
   size; see Section 8.1 as an example.  However, the size of a datagram
   is not authenticated.  That is, if an endpoint receives a datagram of
   a certain size, it cannot know that the sender sent the datagram at
   the same size.  Therefore, an endpoint MUST NOT close a connection
   when it receives a datagram that does not meet size constraints; the
   endpoint MAY discard such datagrams.
requirements.condition: An endpoint receives a datagram that does not meet an applicable size constraint.
requirements.error_behavior: The endpoint may discard the nonconforming datagram.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can deliver a size-nonconforming datagram and observe whether it is discarded without treating discard as a violation.
